chunks: Al-Faqih: Via his chain to Ali ibn Riab, from Abi Basir, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), and Marthad ibn Abi Marthad al-Ghanawi shared a camel between themselves while they were on their way to Badr.

key_terms.بَدْرٍ: Badr, the site of the first major battle in Islam
key_terms.مَرْثَدُ بْنُ أَبِي مَرْثَدٍ الْغَنَوِيُ: Marthad ibn Abi Marthad al-Ghanawi, a companion of the Prophet
key_terms.يَعْقُبُونَ: To take turns (in riding or performing an action)

ai.seo_question: Who shared a camel with the Prophet and Imam Ali during the journey to Badr?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the humility and shared hardship of the Prophet (SAW), Imam Ali (AS), and Marthad ibn Abi Marthad during their journey to Badr, illustrating the practical application of *ta'qib* (taking turns riding a single camel). It serves as a key narrative in Shia scholarship to demonstrate the close spiritual and physical bond between the Ahl al-Bayt and their companions, emphasizing that leadership in Islam is characterized by accessibility and equality in adversity.
